title: Surge-induced scheduler oscillation: slot reservation and lease-damping action plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: After a traffic surge on 2026-02-28 we observed repeated scheduler oscillation across a subset of workers that caused KV-cache churn and transient p95/p99 tail latency spikes for mixed-quant workloads. This ticket tracks containment, a medium-term mitigation (lease damping + slot reservation), and the verification plan for rollout to Dedicated and Hosted clusters.
timeline: 2026-02-28 09:15 UTC: Spike in incoming concurrent requests for model redwood-m-3.2q8 observed in eu-west-1.
2026-02-28 09:17 UTC: Scheduler started speculative probing to alternate kernels; probes amplified due to lack of damping; worker-level slot preemption occurred.
2026-02-28 09:19 UTC: KV cache thrash reported — warmup rates went down and cache miss rates spiked ~6x on affected workers.
2026-02-28 09:25 UTC: Automated autoscaler attempted to add capacity; probe amplification caused new workers to also oscillate briefly.
2026-02-28 09:40 UTC: Emergency rate-limit and abort-probing flag deployed to affected routing layer, stabilizing tail latency.
2026-03-01: Initial triage completed; root cause hypotheses validated via synthetic repro harness (mixed-quant burst pattern).
root_cause: Speculative kernel probing has no global damping across the scheduler; during high arrival rates probes are scheduled indiscriminately causing rapid kernel reassignments.
Worker slot preemption logic allows new probes to evict running batches without a grace lease, causing KV cache eviction and re-warm cycles.
Autoscaler reacts to increased p50/p90 but because probes amplify miss ratios, added capacity temporarily inherits cold caches and continues the cycle.
Workload pattern (many short bursts with mixed-quant models) increases sensitivity to cache warmup and kernel-selection oscillation.
mitigations: Immediate: abort-speculative-probing flag rolled out to routing for eu-west-1 and us-east-1 to stop probe amplification during surge; also applied a temporary request-level concurrency cap.
Short-term (this ticket): implement per-worker lease-damping (exponential backoff for reassign attempts) and a slot-reservation mechanism that prevents probe evictions for running batches.
Medium-term: add global speculative-probe-rate limiter in scheduler that ties probe throughput to observed KV cache warmup metrics.
Long-term: integrate probe-aware autoscaling signal so autoscaler waits for cache-warm progress before shifting traffic to new capacity.
action_items: A1: Implement lease-damping in scheduler to impose backoff on reassignment attempts after a failed probe. Owner: Marco Ruiz. ETA: 2026-03-18. (ENG-246801-A1)
A2: Add slot-reservation flag to worker runtime to prevent evicting actively running batches for speculative probes. Owner: Chen Li. ETA: 2026-03-20. (ENG-246801-A2)
A3: Create a scheduler-level probe-rate limiter that consumes a global token bucket and exposes an override via canary config. Owner: Sofia Becker. ETA: 2026-03-24. (ENG-246801-A3)
A4: Build synthetic regression harness that replays bursty mixed-quant traffic (config + scripts) and add to CI perf-tests. Owner: Ethan Park. ETA: 2026-03-12. (ENG-246801-A4)
A5: Dashboard: add KV-cache warmup metric and probe-caused-eviction counter, link to alerting threshold. Owner: Priya Nambiar (Observability). ETA: 2026-03-15. (ENG-246801-A5)
A6: Canary rollout plan for runtime-1.22 that gates on p95/p99 and KV warmup percentiles (10% -> 30% -> 100%) with manual rollback. Owner: Marco Ruiz. ETA: 2026-03-31. (ENG-246801-A6)
A7: Incident report note and customer communication draft for affected enterprise customers. Owner: Grace Morales (SRE). ETA: 2026-03-05. (ENG-246801-A7)

2026-03-04 Chen Li: Slot-reservation implementation requires small API change in worker RPC; started design doc and backwards-compatible flagging.
2026-03-06 Priya Nambiar: Dashboard panels added to staging; probe-eviction counter shows good fidelity against the synthetic workload.
2026-03-08 Aisha Patel: Prioritized canary rollout; agreed to conservative gating metrics after SRE review.
2026-03-10 Grace Morales: Recommend adding autoscaler-smoothing to the medium-term workstream to avoid churn when adding capacity during warmup.
postmortem_notes: Key lesson: speculative probing must be treated as a distributed rate-limited operation rather than a per-request heuristic in high-concurrency environments.
Operational tweak: add a surge checklist for Support/SRE that proactively flips abort-probing when we see certain arrival-rate signatures.
Verification: all regression harnesses must include KV warmup metrics (miss-rate, served-warm%) in addition to latency percentiles.
notes_for_release: runtime-1.22 will include lease-damping and slot-reservation behind a canary flag. Default disabled until canary passes. Documentation and rollback runbook required before full rollout.
